messages:
jamie: Heads-up — quick check: deciding whether to push routing + quota enforcement to the gateway (edge) or keep it in the control plane/sidecar. Also need route-level telemetry tags for the console. Any strong preferences?

sara: Edge enforcement gives faster rejects and less wasted GPU cycles. Control-plane gives unified visibility and easier rollouts. Main worry is multi-tenant burst fairness.

mike: Edge only works if we propagate stable route/tenant tags. Example headers we'd need:
```
# header example
x-rd-route: inference.v1.generate
x-rd-tenant: acme
```
If tags get lost metrics become useless.

lena: From the console POV we want per-route quota widgets (not just per-tenant). Ops wants 95p latency + token cost per route. Can we attach quota metadata to route defs?

jamie: Yes — route definitions can include quotaPolicy. Enforcement question remains: edge = local token bucket seeded from control plane and periodically sync; sidecar = central check which adds RTT. Edge needs safe fallback.

sara: Local token-bucket is fine if buckets are seeded and refreshed. But we need to handle restore/race when buckets replenish after network partition.

mike: Telemetry requirement: correlate quota hits/fallbacks with trace id. Add x-rd-trace/x-rd-span. Also emit fallback_reason metric (capacity|quota|auth).

lena: Console UX: expose fallback counts, and tie them into canary rollouts. When we flip model variant we need to show delta for quality + cost per route.

jamie: Proposed rollout:
- Phase 0: telemetry-only on 30% of traffic (no enforcement)
- Phase 1: edge enforcement on 10% with strict logging
- Phase 2: increase to 50% if signals look good
- Phase 3: 100% enforcement
Signals: quota_rejections, latency_p95, fallback_rate, cost_per_token.

ops-bot: deploy-bot created canary 'quota-edge-pt1' for service api-gateway — CI lgtm.

sara: One more: protobuf vs JSON. If we push enforcement to edge, using protobuf internally reduces bytes but requires maintaining proto for clients. Maybe gateway accepts JSON and transcodes to proto internally — adds CPU.

mike: Another idea: keep control plane transport-agnostic. Internals speak proto; gateway accepts both JSON/proto and has a fast-path for native proto. Adapter does transcoding only for JSON.

jamie: Good plan. POC: gateway adapter that switches behavior based on x-rd-format header. If proto -> forward raw; if json -> transcode to proto then forward. Collect CPU + latency deltas.

lena: I'll file a console ticket to add per-route quota widget + fallback graph (UX-1234). Will prototype a mock.

jamie: Next steps: mike + sara build the adapter POC and local token-bucket seeding; lena prototype the dashboard; I'll draft the rollout playbook. @sara can you start a short doc with metrics we need? :thumbsup:
